conventions: Primary table: economic cost by month of use. Usage-billed services by usage month, invoiced services by service-period month, one-off purchases and annual fees in the month of purchase.
Prepaid credits count when consumed, not when bought. On shared prepaid accounts (Anthropic, OpenRouter, TypeSafe) Sentinel's share is set FIFO by credit grant.

Reverse-charged VAT (0% on the Twilio, Anthropic, OpenAI and Hetzner invoices) is excluded; whether that VAT is deductible is an open tax question (summary.reverse_charge_vat, outside every total). VAT and fees actually paid (OpenRouter 23% PL VAT and purchase fee; Apple gross price) are included pro rata in the consumed cost.
Free or promotional credit consumed is a zero-cash note line (in_total=false), outside every total.
Accrued unpaid charges (Twilio number rental while suspended) are economic cost of the month they accrue; they are owed, not paid.
No amount is invented. Estimates carry evidence_class 'estimate', a method and low/high bounds.
Secondary table: cash by payment date, Sentinel share only; a purchase and its consumption are never added together.
Current monthly cost: usage services = Oct 1-14 daily average x 30.44; fixed fees at their monthly price; annual fees / 12; services no longer used = 0. Scenario lines stay outside the total.

FX: NBP table A mid rate. Lines: last business day of the usage month (latest available day for the partial current month). Cash events: last business day before the payment date. Current monthly cost: latest available day.
Excluded: the owner's time, Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions, Codex and other cross-project coding tools, the msigalert/InfoCentral product and other projects.

operational_risks.text: Sentinel was blind for about 61 hours, from 2026-09-17 10:07 UTC to 2026-09-19 23:19 UTC. The shared Anthropic prepaid credit hit zero and every Haiku call failed with HTTP 400 'credit balance too low' (689 classification and 329 vagueness-check errors in the journal). No article was classified in that window, so no urgency 9-10 alert could have fired. Service came back only when the owner bought $20 by hand at 23:16 UTC.

Root cause: auto-reload failed and Anthropic paused it on Aug 18, and again on Sep 13 when the card was declined for insufficient funds. After Sep 13 nothing refilled the balance. The 'credit balance is low' warning ($2.19, Sep 15) and the 'API access is turned off' email (Sep 17) both reached the owner's mailbox and were later trashed by the 2026-10-01/02 mail cleanup. No spend notification is configured in the Console today. A $100 monthly API-spend threshold notice did exist and fired on 2026-05-27, so that setting was later removed or replaced by the $150 org spend limit. Either way it warned about spending, not about a low balance.

Shared balance: other projects draw on the same prepaid pool. On May 20-21 the MemSearch backfill burned $86.47 in about 16 hours and would have emptied the balance if the $150 had not been bought. A burst from any other key can starve Sentinel whenever Sentinel runs on Anthropic.

Rollback exposure today: Sentinel does not currently depend on Anthropic. But the legacy Haiku path is still wired and is also the code default in sentinel/config.py, and the Sentinel key is still active. A rollback would start on a shared $18.77 balance, about 5.6 days at today's volume (~$3.38/day at Haiku list price). It would then rely on auto-reload (below $10, top up to $20) with the same card that declined twice. The org spend limit of $150/month covers the central rollback estimate (~$103/month) and the busiest October week (~$118/month) plus msigalert. It does not cover the high bound with the tokenizer allowance (~$153/month); in that case Sentinel classification would stop late in the month when the limit is hit.

Mail-cleanup risk: the 2026-10-02 cleanup trashed at least 19 Anthropic billing emails, including the low-balance and access-off warnings. Future warnings may vanish the same way before the owner sees them. Since Sep 19 the billing entity is Anthropic Ireland, which sends from a different Stripe sender, so any mail filter keyed on the old sender will miss its receipts and failure notices.

Credit expiry: the remaining $18.77 expires about 2027-09-20. At msigalert's ~$0.52/month, roughly $12-13 would expire unused. This is a minor cash leak, not a Sentinel cost unless Sentinel uses the credit.

The API credit balance was $0.77 at 18:03 UTC on 2026-10-14. Auto-reload is OFF: OpenAI turned it off itself after the card charge failed at 18:44 UTC on 2026-10-08. The owner then topped up $20.00 by card at about 20:15 UTC on 2026-10-14 (OpenAI funding email), so the end-of-day balance is about $20.65 ($20.62-20.67) instead of about $0.65. At $0.61 a day (October average) to $0.88 a day (Oct 13) that is about 23-34 days of use, to roughly 7-17 November once the project cap is raised. The balance is therefore no longer the first limit: the $10 project cap (next item) stops classification first. When either runs out, OpenAI rejects requests, classification pauses, articles stay pending, and urgency 9-10 alerts can be missed. Resolved 2026-10-14: after the owner's $20.00 top-up, the portal billing overview showed an API credit balance of $20.70 at about 2026-10-14 21:00 UTC. Auto-reload is now ON: when the balance falls to $5, it reloads to $20, with no monthly cap on automatic reloads. The card has not yet been proven on an automatic charge since the 2026-10-08 failure; if it fails again at the $5 trigger, OpenAI switches auto-reload off and the remaining $5 lasts only about 6-8 days ($0.61-0.88 a day).

Project Sentinel has an enforced hard spend limit of $10 a month. About $8.53 ($8.51-8.56) will have been used by the end of 2026-10-14 UTC, which leaves about $1.47. At $0.61-0.88 a day the cap is reached between about 16:00 UTC on 2026-10-16 and 10:00 UTC on 2026-10-17. Requests then fail until the reset on 1 November, even with credit on the balance. A top-up alone does NOT fix this. The cap must be raised to at least about $25, or to the app allowance of $30. The run-rate ($18.54 a month, high bound $20.88) is above the cap, so without a change this would happen again every month around day 15-20. Resolved 2026-10-14: the owner raised the Project Sentinel monthly spend limit from $10 to $30 (still 'Limit enforced'); the portal showed $8.48 / $30.00 at about 2026-10-14 22:00 UTC. The existing $10 spend alert (now 33% of the cap) was kept as an early warning. The new cap is above the run-rate and its high bound, so normal volume no longer stops classification mid-month. It equals the app's own $30 budget, so a heavy incident month can still reach it (see the app-budget risk).

The 2026-10-08 auto-recharge failed on the card used for the 2026 OpenAI purchases. Anthropic payments also failed on 2026-09-19 and 2026-10-04. A card problem across providers can silently stop prepaid LLM funding. Re-enable auto-reload only with a card that works.

Sentinel's own app budget is $30 a month (classification.budget). Normal volume uses about $15.6-20.9 a month and is rising. A real incident that sends several times the usual article volume for some days could reach the $30 cap. Classification would then pause exactly when alerts matter.

The OpenAI funding receipts of 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-29 were trashed by the 2026-10-01/02 mail cleanup. Make sure the cleanup never trashes OpenAI billing warnings (auto-recharge failed, low balance, spend-limit alerts). They are the only early signal before classification stops.
Neither OpenRouter nor TypeSafe is in the live alert path. The production classifier calls OpenAI directly, so credit exhaustion or key expiry on these two accounts cannot stop alerts.
The Sentinel OpenRouter evaluation key is Expired (limit $50, usage $3.263). Any rerun of the offline model comparison will fail until the owner makes a new key. There is no production effect.

Those notices are the early warning before alerts stop.

Urgency 9-10 phone calls are not being delivered.

A recharge first pays the debt before any call or SMS can go out: USD 9.4924 until 2026-10-20, USD 10.6424 from 2026-10-21 and USD 14.6424 from 2026-10-28. At scenario A pace (about USD 18.03 usage + 5.15 rentals = about USD 23.18 a month; about USD 37.42 at the high bound) a top-up of USD 50 on top of the debt lasts roughly 2 months (about 1.3 months at the high bound), less in an alert storm. Earlier suspensions ended when a manual top-up brought the balance positive.

Six earlier suspensions stopped all SMS and calls; each began 30 seconds to 3.5 minutes after the last accepted send, so Sentinel's own traffic emptied the balance. Outage windows (UTC): 2026-04-20 12:57 to 04-25 18:52 (about 5.2 days); 05-09 10:47 to 05-17 15:07 (about 8.2 days); 05-20 00:56 to 05-22 15:36 (about 2.6 days); 05-25 00:31 to 15:10 (about 15 hours); 05-29 02:42 to 18:01 (about 15 hours, which caused a missed urgency-9 call: five retries rejected 03:40-17:42); 06-02 18:11 to 06-03 11:14 (about 17 hours).

Auto-recharge (refill to about USD 20) worked from 2026-03-21 to 2026-04-10, then failed on 2026-04-17 (USD 10.23) and 2026-04-20 (USD 20.17) because the payment could not be processed. It is not configured now, so after any recharge the account will suspend again whenever the balance reaches zero; the only warning is the default low-balance email below USD 5.

Small manual top-ups lasted only days at pre-June volumes: USD 20 on 05-22 was gone by 05-25, and USD 20 on 05-25 by 05-29. Polish alert SMS are UCS-2 encoded (about 10.5 segments, roughly USD 0.48 per SMS), so SMS volume drains the balance fast.

The balance grows more negative by USD 5.15 a month with number renewals (US on the 21st, PL on the 28th). If Twilio eventually releases the numbers for non-payment, the Polish sender number may be lost and the sender configuration would have to change.
Only one card is on file now (a Visa); the two earlier cards are gone. A failed card payment stopped alerts in April.

Card on file: Hetzner auto-debits every invoice from a credit card. If the card expires, is blocked or hits its limit, Hetzner's dunning ends in a server lock, and then every alert stops, including urgency 9-10. The billing mail goes to the owner's main Gmail. The owner's mail cleanup trashed all earlier Hetzner billing mail on 2026-10-02, so a payment-failure warning could be missed if cleanup rules touch Hetzner mail.

Single point of failure: the one CX23 server is the whole production system. Hetzner Backups and snapshots are off, and the DB backups sit on the same disk. The Hetzner account has no two-factor authentication. A compromised account or a disk loss would stop alerts and lose the database. Turning on Hetzner Backups would cost about 20% of the server price, by Hetzner's published rule (not verified in this audit).

Price changes: the server bills the legacy CX23 price of EUR 3.99 + 0.50 per month. Since 2026-06-15, new CX23 orders and rescales cost EUR 5.49/month by Hetzner's price-adjustment page, which also warns that some changes to legacy-priced servers switch them to current prices. Deleting and rebuilding, or rescaling, would therefore raise the server line by about EUR 1.50 per month (the IPv4 price under current terms was not checked). Being on a legacy price does not protect the server from every increase: Hetzner already repriced this running server once, from EUR 0.0048/h in March to a EUR 3.99 monthly price from April, so the run-rate can change without any action by the owner.
No spend alerts: the Console's usage 'E-Mail Warning' boxes are unchecked for all projects. The risk is low, because the server is capped at EUR 4.49 per month and uses 0 of its 20 TB of traffic.

Apple licence agreement: an updated Apple Developer Program License Agreement must be accepted at developer.apple.com/account by 2026-11-13 (notice of 2026-10-14). The developer portal banner already says that access to Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles, App Store Connect and its API stays blocked until the owner accepts it. Until then, no new iOS build and no APNs key or profile work for the Sentinel push app is possible. Whether existing push delivery keeps working meanwhile was not verified.

Apple auto-renew is OFF, and the membership ends on 2027-06-01. Without a manual renewal (429 zł list fee), the developer team lapses. The iPhone app then cannot be rebuilt or re-signed, and push to it will probably stop.

Even with renewal, the iPhone runs an internal 'preview' build signed on 2026-06-03/04. Ad-hoc provisioning profiles and distribution certificates are typically valid for about one year. A fresh EAS build is therefore likely needed around early June 2027, before that build stops launching. The build needs an active membership and an accepted licence agreement.

Expo push is currently the only alert channel that delivers. Tiers 5-8 are push-only by design, and the unfunded Twilio account makes every call and SMS for tiers 9-10 fail. A lapse of the Apple membership, the licence agreement or the free Expo account would therefore silence every tier. Push is also not a wake-up for tiers 9-10, because the Critical Alerts entitlement is still pending.

Notices go astray. The Apple order email and invoice were deleted in the 2026-10-02 mail cleanup. No Expo email exists in any searched mailbox, because the Expo account uses Google SSO through an unidentified address. Renewal or agreement deadlines like the 2026-11-13 one can therefore be missed.

The Expo Free plan limits carry no cost risk. Usage is far below them (0 of 30 builds and 0 of 1,000 update users this period), and push has no quota charge. No spend cap or suspension on the Expo billing side can stop alerts.

Sentinel has no external uptime monitor; this is a zero-cost gap, not a charge. Its only built-in failure notices (pipeline failed several cycles in a row, a source down for many cycles) are sent by Twilio SMS in sentinel/scheduler.py, and every Twilio SMS fails with HTTP 401 while the account is unfunded. The account has been suspended for low balance since 2026-08-23 17:21 UTC; 2026-09-21 is only the first error retained in the server log. A crash, a Hetzner suspension, or exhausted OpenAI credit would therefore show up only as missing push alerts. A free heartbeat check would close the gap at USD 0; msigalert's runbook says its Better Stack free plan uses 9 of 10 monitors.

All backups (daily SQLite copies kept 7 days, plus pre-deploy copies) sit on the VPS's own disk, and Hetzner Backups and snapshots are off (console, 2026-10-14). If the Hetzner account were suspended for non-payment or the disk failed, the service and its backups would be lost together.

risks.title: Twilio: telefon przy najpilniejszym alercie dziś nie zadzwoni
risks.text: Od 23.08.2026, 17:21 UTC konto Twilio jest zawieszone z braku środków i dziś celowo niedoładowane. Żadne połączenie ani SMS nie wychodzi; od 15.09.2026 dziennik pokazuje 290 odrzuconych połączeń i tyle samo SMS-ów. Dotyczyły one tylko 48 zdarzeń najwyższej pilności: na zawieszonym koncie żadne zdarzenie nie zostaje potwierdzone, a odrzucone połączenie nie zostawia śladu, więc system ponawia próby wielokrotnie. Dług na koncie wynosi 9,49 USD i rośnie o 5,15 USD miesięcznie za dwa numery: do 10,64 USD po odnowieniu 21.10.2026 i do 14,64 USD po odnowieniu 28.10.2026. Doładowanie najpierw spłaci dług. Przy obecnych zasadach wysyłki zużycie po doładowaniu, liczone od liczby zdarzeń, a nie prób, to około 18,03 USD miesięcznie (przedział 16,83 USD – 32,27 USD) plus numery.

risks.title: OpenAI: limit podniesiony, doładowanie włączone, karta niesprawdzona
risks.text: Wieczorem 14.10.2026 podniosłeś twardy limit miesięczny projektu Sentinel w OpenAI z 10,00 USD do 30,00 USD; panel pokazywał wtedy 8,48 USD z 30,00 USD (14.10.2026, 22:00 UTC). Nowy limit jest wyższy niż bieżące tempo 18,54 USD miesięcznie i jego górna granica 20,88 USD, więc przy zwykłej liczbie artykułów klasyfikacja nie stanie już w połowie miesiąca. Październik zamknie się na około 18,88 USD przy średnim tempie (0,61 USD dziennie) i na około 23,49 USD przy najwyższym dziennym zużyciu (0,88 USD). Powiadomienie o wydatkach przy 10,00 USD zostało jako wczesne ostrzeżenie. Limit równa się teraz własnemu budżetowi aplikacji, więc prawdziwy kryzys z wielokrotnie większą liczbą artykułów nadal może go wyczerpać. Saldo po doładowaniu z 14.10.2026, 20:15 UTC (20,00 USD) wynosiło 20,70 USD (14.10.2026, 21:00 UTC). Automatyczne doładowanie jest znowu włączone: gdy saldo spadnie do 5,00 USD, OpenAI doładuje je do 20,00 USD, bez miesięcznego limitu doładowań. Karta nie przeszła jednak jeszcze automatycznego obciążenia od nieudanej płatności 08.10.2026. Gdyby znów została odrzucona, OpenAI wyłączy doładowanie przy saldzie 5,00 USD, a to starczy na około 8,2 dnia przy średnim tempie i 5,7 dnia przy najwyższym zużyciu.

risks.title: Jeden serwer i brak zewnętrznego monitoringu
risks.text: Cały Sentinel działa na jednym serwerze Hetzner. Kopie bazy leżą na tym samym dysku, a kopie zapasowe Hetznera są wyłączone. Nic z zewnątrz nie sprawdza, czy Sentinel działa: awaria byłaby widoczna tylko jako brak powiadomień. Własny budżet aplikacji na OpenAI to 30,00 USD miesięcznie; prawdziwy kryzys z dużą liczbą artykułów może go wyczerpać.

open_items: Twilio nie rozliczyło połączeń alarmowych z lipca i sierpnia. Gdyby je doliczyło, doszłoby około 5,16 USD (poza sumą). Zaległe opłaty za numery (9,15 USD) wyliczono z salda w panelu; potwierdzi je październikowy wyciąg.

Październikowej faktury Hetznera jeszcze nie ma; do tego czasu październik to naliczenie (2,42 EUR).
Darmowy plan Expo odczytano w panelu, ale bez zrzutu ekranu.
Zakup w KartotekaOnline.pl (329,67 zł, 03.09.2026) ma nieznany cel. Domyślnie nie jest kosztem Sentinela; potwierdź.
Przy płatnościach w obcej walucie rzeczywisty koszt w złotych zależy od kursu i prowizji Twojego banku. Raport używa kursów NBP; wyciągi z karty dałyby dokładne kwoty.
method: Koszt liczę według miesiąca zużycia. Usługi płatne za zużycie trafiają do miesiąca zużycia, faktury do miesiąca, którego dotyczą, a opłaty jednorazowe i roczne do miesiąca zakupu.

Kredyty kupione z góry liczę dopiero wtedy, gdy zostaną zużyte. Na kontach wspólnych z innymi projektami (Anthropic, OpenRouter, TypeSafe) Sentinel dostaje tylko swoją część; najstarszy kredyt zużywa się pierwszy.

VAT pomijam tam, gdzie rozlicza się go odwrotnie (zero na fakturze: Twilio, Anthropic, OpenAI i Hetzner). Tam, gdzie VAT i opłaty faktycznie zapłaciłeś (OpenRouter, Apple), są w koszcie. Czy pominięty VAT możesz odliczyć, to otwarte pytanie podatkowe w części „Pytania i decyzje”.
Darmowe kredyty pokazuję jako notatkę bez gotówki, poza sumą. Opłaty naliczone, ale niezapłacone (numery Twilio w czasie zawieszenia), są kosztem miesiąca, w którym je naliczono.
Nie zgaduję kwot. Każdy szacunek jest oznaczony i ma opisaną metodę oraz przedział.

Koszt miesięczny teraz: usługi za zużycie to średnia dzienna od 01.10.2026 do 14.10.2026 razy 30,44 (przeciętna liczba dni w miesiącu); opłaty stałe po cenie miesięcznej; opłaty roczne podzielone na dwanaście; usługi już nieużywane to zero.
